meta.title: Microsoft Fake Sign-In Sites Catalog
meta.purpose: Defensive blocklist of LIVE URLs impersonating Microsoft sign-in pages (Microsoft 365, Outlook, Azure AD / Entra ID, Live) for blocking, detection engineering and threat hunting.
meta.warning: URLs are REAL and UNDEFANGED. Do not visit or submit credentials — consume them in blocklists and hunting queries only. Refreshed hourly; rolling retention window.

entries.technique: Credential harvester on a compromised legitimate host, faking an OAuth authorize request with a capital-I 'redirect_urI' parameter pointing at login.microsoftonline.com
entries.detection: Proxy/URL hunt for query strings containing 'redirect_urI' (capital i) or 'sso_reload=true' on non-Microsoft hostnames — the real parameter is 'redirect_uri' and only appears on login.microsoftonline.com

entries.technique: Brandjacked .ms domain masquerading as a Microsoft authentication endpoint; per-victim 'E.<token>' path serves an MFA/confirm-identity credential prompt
entries.detection: Block the apex domain authentication.ms and hunt for URI paths matching the regex /E\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{12,}/ across authentication.ms, multi-factor.link, auth.properties and signin.broker

entries.technique: Outlook 'notification' credential page on Tencent EdgeOne Pages free hosting, using a long keyword-stuffed label plus random suffix to defeat string blocklists
entries.detection: Treat *.edgeone.dev as an unsanctioned hosting provider (same class as *.pages.dev / *.workers.dev); flag labels >40 chars that concatenate office/outlook/notification keywords before a random 12-char suffix

entries.technique: Replit-hosted 'security server' fake sign-in kit; the --<operator> suffix is the attacker's Replit account name, so each actor mass-produces near-identical pages
entries.detection: Regex the proxy logs for ^https?://(security-server|server-security)[a-z-]*--[a-z0-9-]+\.replit\.app — the kit name is stable while the operator handle rotates

entries.technique: Same Replit 'security-server' Microsoft sign-in kit under a different operator handle
entries.detection: Block *.replit.app wholesale if unused, or alert on any Replit app whose HTML references login.microsoftonline.com assets or aadcdn.msftauth.net

entries.technique: Replit 'security-server-page' variant of the same Microsoft credential-harvest kit
entries.detection: Pivot on favicon/HTML hash of one confirmed security-server--* page in urlscan.io to enumerate the rest of the cluster before they are reported

entries.technique: Free-hosting abuse — credential-harvest page on attacker-created Vercel subdomain; page title is literally "Microsoft"
entries.detection: Alert on outbound HTTPS to *.vercel.app subdomains containing 'microsoft'/'office'/'outlook' tokens; these are never Microsoft-owned

entries.technique: Compromised legitimate site hosting the reused 'onedrive-verify-obf' obfuscated HTML credential kit
entries.detection: Hunt proxy/web logs for any URI path ending in 'onedrive-verify-obf.html' — a fixed kit filename reused across many hacked hosts

entries.technique: Subdomain squatting on a compromised German domain; label is misspelled 'clovd-micrsotf-mail' plus random hex padding
entries.detection: Flag DNS for long (>30 char) single-label subdomains mixing a misspelled 'microsoft'/'micrsotf' string with random alphanumerics under unrelated TLDs

entries.technique: Typosquat of 'microsoftonline' with an inserted hyphen on a .gr ccTLD
entries.detection: Regex newly-registered-domain feeds for /micro-?soft-?online/ on any TLD outside microsoft.com's registered set

entries.technique: Brand-concatenation typosquat ('microsoftoffice' + 'o365') used as a sign-in lure domain
entries.detection: Alert on domains combining two Microsoft brand tokens (microsoft/office/o365/m365) joined by a hyphen — Microsoft does not register these patterns

entries.technique: Homoglyph/typosquat ('miccrossofteam' = Microsoft Teams) on a cheap .top TLD, served over plain HTTP
entries.detection: Fuzzy-match (Levenshtein <=3) registered domains against 'microsoftteams'; prioritize .top/.xyz/.cfd TLDs and HTTP-only listeners

entries.technique: Weebly free-site abuse with a French-language lure ('connexion compte Outlook' = Outlook account sign-in)
entries.detection: Block/alert on *.weebly.com and *.weeblysite.com hostnames whose label contains outlook/hotmail/microsoft/office — a persistently abused free-hosting pattern

entries.technique: Spanish-language 'verify your account' credential-harvest page on free zya.me subdomain host, homoglyph 'micros0ft'
entries.detection: Alert on outbound HTTP POST to *.zya.me / *.yzz.me / *.hstn.me — free ByetHost-family hosts have no legitimate enterprise use

entries.technique: Typosquat brand-in-domain-label credential page behind Cloudflare; flagged young domain
entries.detection: Hunt newly-registered .site/.online/.live TLDs containing 'microsoft'+'office365' in CT logs; block at DNS before first click

entries.technique: Typosquat of 'microsoft teams' (dropped space/letter shuffle) serving fake Teams/M365 sign-in
entries.detection: Regex edit-distance <=2 against 'microsoftteams' on newly observed domains in proxy logs

entries.technique: Microsoft Forms-themed lure domain redirecting to cloned Entra ID sign-in
entries.detection: Any hostname matching ^(forms|inbox|protect|urgent|salessupport)-microsoft\. is not Microsoft — Microsoft Forms only lives on forms.office.com / forms.cloud.microsoft

entries.technique: Typosquat sign-in-verification lure, newly registered lookalike
entries.detection: CT-log monitor for certs with SAN containing 'login'+'microsoft'+'verify'; legitimate Microsoft sign-in is only login.microsoftonline.com

entries.technique: Typosquat of account.live.com using .live TLD as the brand suffix
entries.detection: Flag domains where a Microsoft service name is the SLD and the TLD mimics the real hostname's subdomain (account.live.com vs microsoft-account.live)

entries.technique: Passkey/security-key registration lure — same theme as the Storm-3121/Storm-3032 passkey cluster
entries.detection: Extend existing passkey-phish blocklist regex to (passkey|key|mfa|sso)-?(microsoft|os)\.(com|online|live)

entries.technique: Brand-plus-suffix typosquat landing page for OWA credential capture
entries.detection: Block newly-registered domains prefixed 'office365' outside microsoft.com/office.com zones

entries.technique: Fake Teams meeting-invite lure leading to M365 sign-in page (same pattern as msteamsinvitees.com)
entries.detection: Hunt 'teams*invite*' domains in mail URL-rewrite logs; real invites resolve to teams.microsoft.com / teams.live.com

entries.technique: Hotmail typosquat on cheap .site TLD
entries.detection: Alert on any non-microsoft.com/live.com domain whose page title contains 'Hotmail' or 'Outlook' sign-in strings

entries.technique: 'New message in your inbox' notification lure to fake OWA logon
entries.detection: Block domains concatenating outlook+inbox/message/mail tokens; correlate with inbound mail subjects referencing undelivered messages

entries.technique: Teams invite typosquat, sibling of microsofteamsinvite.top on the same registration burst
entries.detection: Cluster-block the whole microsofteamsinvite.* family across TLDs

entries.technique: Pluralized-brand typosquat ('microsofts') fake Teams meeting join page
entries.detection: Detect plural/possessive brand mutations: microsofts, microsoftt, micosoft in proxy SNI

entries.technique: Fake Teams download page (variant of the known teams-microsoft-download.com)
entries.detection: Already-known sibling teams-microsoft-download.com — block the singular/plural pair together

entries.technique: Bare-brand squat on a low-reputation TLD used for webmail credential pages
entries.detection: Deny-list bare Microsoft product names on non-Microsoft TLDs (.surf, .sbs, .cfd, .shop, .day, .baby)

entries.technique: Fake 'shared document' OneDrive lure fronting an M365 sign-in prompt
entries.detection: OneDrive sharing only occurs on *.sharepoint.com / 1drv.ms / onedrive.live.com — alert on any other host serving a OneDrive-branded document viewer

entries.technique: OneDrive brand-plus-suffix squat registered in the same batch as onedriveshare.net
entries.detection: Same registrar/nameserver pivot as onedriveshare.net — block the pair and monitor the hosting ASN

entries.technique: Tech-support-themed lure escalating to Microsoft account sign-in
entries.detection: Pair with existing microsoft-techsupport.com blocks; flag any 'support'+'microsoft' domain not under support.microsoft.com

entries.technique: Hyphenated brand-pair typosquat hosting a OneDrive document-access sign-in
entries.detection: Regex ^microsoft-(onedrive|sharepoint|teams|office)\. across all TLDs — none are Microsoft-owned

entries.technique: Mailbox-notification lure domain for OWA credential capture
entries.detection: Match ^(inbox|mail|webmail)-microsoft\. in SNI/DNS; no legitimate Microsoft mail host uses that form

entries.technique: Homoglyph typosquat (zero-for-O) OneDrive file-share phishing page
entries.detection: Normalize 0→o and 1→l on observed domains before comparing to a Microsoft brand list; catches 0utl00k/0nedrive families

entries.technique: Fake Microsoft sales/support contact page routing to an Entra ID credential prompt
entries.detection: Any hostname ending '-microsoft.com' is a squat — the real zone is microsoft.com with brand as the SLD

entries.technique: 'Protect your mailbox' security-alert lure to fake Outlook sign-in
entries.detection: Correlate DNS hits with inbound mail containing 'unusual sign-in activity' subject lines

entries.technique: Fake OWA 'access portal' credential-harvest page
entries.detection: Hunt POSTs to hosts with 'portal'+'outlook'/'owa' tokens; legitimate OWA is outlook.office.com / outlook.office365.com

entries.technique: Reversed-label squat designed to read as 'onedrive.com' in truncated mobile URL bars
entries.detection: Flag domains beginning 'com-' — a classic mobile URL-bar truncation trick; sibling of known com-onedrive-microsoftonline.com

entries.technique: Subdomain of an active phishing estate (evergreenfin.ltd) serving a fake Outlook/OWA sign-in page
entries.detection: Hunt for any DNS/proxy resolution to *.evergreenfin.ltd — the same estate already hosts office., onelogin. and xn--knto-55d. subdomains; block the apex, not individual hosts

entries.technique: Homoglyph typosquat (zero-for-o) of 'microsoftoffice365' hosting a credential-harvest sign-in clone
entries.detection: Regex outbound HTTP Host and email links for microsoft/office brand strings containing digits 0/1 substituted for o/l

entries.technique: Typosquat of login.microsoftonline.com on a low-cost .top TLD
entries.detection: Alert on any resolved domain containing 'microsoftonline' that is not *.microsoftonline.com; flag .top/.xyz/.sbs TLDs registered <30 days

entries.technique: Reversed-label typosquat ('com-' prefix) mimicking a OneDrive share notification landing page
entries.detection: Flag hostnames that begin with 'com-' or 'www-' followed by a brand token — a reliable reversed-FQDN squat signal

entries.technique: Doubled-character typosquat of 'outlook' on a cheap .site TLD
entries.detection: Levenshtein distance <=2 against 'outlook'/'microsoft'/'onedrive' over newly observed domains in proxy logs

entries.technique: Target-tailored webmail lure — victim org name appended to 'outlook-email-' for a bespoke OWA sign-in clone
entries.detection: Hunt registrations matching ^(outlook|owa|mail)-.*-?<yourcompany> — set a CT-log watch on your own brand name paired with Microsoft tokens

entries.technique: Brand-squat document-share lure funnelling to a Microsoft credential prompt
entries.detection: Block newly registered .xyz/.top domains containing 'microsoft' at the egress proxy by default

entries.technique: Exact-brand-plus-suffix squat on .top TLD
entries.detection: Domain age <7 days + exact 'microsoft' substring + non-Microsoft registrar = auto-block candidate

entries.technique: Brand-plus-word squat used as an account-services / sign-in landing page
entries.detection: Watch CT logs for certificates issued to 'microsoft'+generic-suffix .com names not owned by Microsoft Corp

entries.technique: Character-transposition typosquat ('olnine' for 'online') of login.microsoftonline.com
entries.detection: Run a transposition/bitsquat generator against 'microsoftonline' and preload the results into DNS RPZ

entries.technique: Entra-themed brand squat impersonating an identity/SSO re-enrolment portal
entries.detection: Alert on any non-Microsoft domain containing 'entra' — rare token, very low false-positive rate

entries.technique: Teams 'update required' lure leading to a Microsoft sign-in prompt
entries.detection: Flag domains combining 'teams'/'team' with update|setup|invite|download tokens registered in the last 30 days

entries.technique: Brand squat with regional suffix hosting an Office 365 credential page
entries.detection: Match 'microsoftoffice' as a contiguous substring in any non-microsoft.com host

entries.technique: Homoglyph typosquat (zero-for-O) of OneDrive — sibling of the already-tracked 0nedrive.space
entries.detection: Normalise 0->o and 1->l in observed hostnames, then re-match against your brand list

entries.technique: AiTM credential proxy on free .mm.am subdomain; spoofs Entra OAuth query string with capital-I 'redirect_urI' homoglyph
entries.detection: Hunt proxy/DNS for the literal parameter 'redirect_urI=' (capital i) and for client_id 4765445b-32c6-49b0-83e6-1d93765276ca on any host that is not login.microsoftonline.com — same kit as the earlier acltci.com node

entries.technique: Typosquat domain stacking 'com-microsoftonline-ondrive' to make the brand read left-to-right in the hostname
entries.detection: Alert on newly registered domains containing 'microsoftonline' as a label substring rather than as the registrable domain; also flag the 'ondrive' misspelling

entries.technique: Lookalike parent domain microsoft-ssl.com with trust-signal subdomain serving fake security-notification sign-in
entries.detection: Block the whole microsoft-ssl.com zone and hunt NRD registrations combining 'microsoft' with security words (ssl, secure, cert, verify) as hyphenated parent domains

entries.technique: Tech-support-themed credential page on numbered clickN.* redirector subdomains
entries.detection: Wildcard-block *.microsoftsupportcenter.digital — enumerated click1..clickN subdomains rotate; this extends the known click5/click6 nodes

entries.technique: Typosquat host on the free yzz.me dynamic-hosting service
entries.detection: Treat *.yzz.me as high-risk for Microsoft-themed phishing (third observed node after validar-micuenta-outlook and loginemailservices); block the TLD-level provider for corporate egress

entries.technique: Free Vercel app-hosting abuse serving a cloned Microsoft sign-in SPA
entries.detection: Flag *.vercel.app hostnames whose project slug contains microsoft/outlook/onedrive/office; legitimate Microsoft never serves auth from vercel.app

entries.technique: Vercel-hosted fake Outlook Web Access logon
entries.detection: Same Vercel slug heuristic; 'serv'/'srv' + brand token is a recurring naming pattern in this cluster

entries.technique: Vercel-hosted fake OneDrive document-share gate harvesting M365 credentials
entries.detection: Match Vercel projects with brand + numeric-word padding (4-nine, 2-five); pair with Referer analysis from mail gateways

entries.technique: www-prefixed variant of the same Vercel OneDrive lure (separate live submission)
entries.detection: Block the apex and www variant together — Vercel resolves both; wildcard the project slug, not the single FQDN

entries.technique: AI app-builder PaaS abuse (bolt.host / Bolt.new) hosting a generated Office 365 logon clone
entries.detection: Add bolt.host to the PaaS watchlist alongside replit.app/vercel.app/workers.dev; alert on *.bolt.host containing office/microsoft/outlook plus a random alphanumeric suffix

entries.technique: Compromised legitimate WordPress/CMS site hosting a static outlook.html credential-harvest page
entries.detection: Hunt web-proxy logs for static filenames outlook.html / office365.html / onedrive-verify*.html on unrelated business domains — same TTP as the intermezzoconsultoria.com.br and creyt.cl nodes

entries.technique: Free Blogspot subdomain abuse serving a Word document-view lure that pivots to a fake M365 sign-in
entries.detection: Alert on *.blogspot.com hostnames containing microsoft/outlook/office — recurring free-platform cluster with jimdofree.com and weebly.com nodes

entries.technique: Static credential-harvest clone of the Microsoft sign-in page hosted free on GitHub Pages
entries.detection: Alert on outbound HTTP to *.github.io paths containing /microsoft, /office, /owa — no legitimate Entra ID auth ever lands on github.io

entries.technique: Typosquatted GitHub Pages org name ('outlook-login') serving a Spanish-language OWA credential form
entries.detection: Hunt proxy logs for github.io subdomains whose label contains outlook/login/signin; also flag GitHub Pages referers preceding POSTs to non-Microsoft hosts

entries.technique: PhaaS kit using an /i/<32-hex> victim-ID path on an Azure-hosted lookalike subdomain (office365.* on an unrelated apex)
entries.detection: Regex URL path ^/i/[0-9a-f]{32,33}$ on non-Microsoft hosts resolving to 20.50.64.14 — one shared kit across several of today's domains

entries.technique: Typosquat apex m365-microsoft.com with rotating service subdomains (support/security/programme-hup/emailnotifications)
entries.detection: Block the whole m365-microsoft.com apex plus any new subdomain under it; the apex is not Microsoft-owned and all labels resolve to 20.50.64.14

entries.technique: Same /i/<hex> PhaaS kit, French-language ('programme') lure subdomain on the m365-microsoft.com typosquat
entries.detection: Wildcard-block *.m365-microsoft.com; alert on first-seen subdomains of a domain already flagged for credential phishing

entries.technique: Mail-notification-themed subdomain of the m365-microsoft.com typosquat, cleartext HTTP credential post
entries.detection: Flag any plaintext HTTP request to a host containing 'microsoft' — Microsoft enforces HSTS, so HTTP to an MS-branded host is phishing by definition

entries.technique: Homoglyph typosquat 'rricrosoft' (rn→m substitution) running the same /i/<hex> kit
entries.detection: Fuzzy-match registered domains against 'microsoft' with rn/m, vv/w, l/I substitutions; same 20.50.64.14 infrastructure cluster

entries.technique: Security-alert lure on an email-microsoft.com typosquat; short opaque token path consistent with an AiTM relay
entries.detection: Host resolves into 212.104.128.0/24 — the same /24 as the auth.properties AiTM cluster; block that netblock and alert on any MS-branded hostname in it

entries.technique: AiTM reverse proxy (Tycoon2FA-style) — 'E.<base64 token>' path with a fake /microsoftonline/mailbox/upgrade query decoration to steal session cookies
entries.detection: Regex ^/E\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}$ on any non-Microsoft host; this family rotates across authentication.ms, multi-factor.link, signin.broker, auth.properties — block the pattern, not the domain

entries.technique: 'Mailbox alert' kit with /s/<campaign>/<id>/<UUID> routing path and an outlook.* subdomain on an attacker apex
entries.detection: Hunt the literal campaign ID 63bzgfsvbwsfcdx7y9 and the path shape /s/<alnum18>/<hex6>/<uuid> — identical URI is live on at least two rotating domains

entries.technique: Domain-rotation twin of the webaccess-alert.com kit — byte-identical path, different apex, MFA/token-verification lure
entries.detection: Pivot on the shared URI to discover sibling domains; alert on any new apex with an 'outlook' subdomain serving path prefix /s/63bzgfsvbwsfcdx7y9/

entries.technique: SPA phishing kit — the ~900-char prefilled victim token sits in the URL fragment (#) so it never reaches the server log, with type=onedrive selecting the brand skin
entries.detection: Alert on URLs >500 chars containing '#/main?type=' with a token= fragment; fragment-carried state defeats proxy URL logging, so inspect full-URI browser telemetry

entries.technique: Userinfo-spoof (@) URL — 'hotmail.com-...' placed before the @ so the real host is a GoDaddy shared-hosting IP; target address prefilled via ?email=
entries.detection: Flag any URL containing '@' in the authority where the userinfo includes a known brand string; also alert on ?email= prefill parameters to non-corporate hosts

entries.technique: Deceptive-subdomain stacking — 'login.microsoftonline-billing-verification-secured-help' is only a label on cpanel.site, billing-suspension lure
entries.detection: Alert when 'login.microsoftonline' appears as a subdomain label rather than as the registrable domain; eTLD+1 of cpanel.site is never Microsoft

entries.technique: Spanish 'reactivate your account' lure on free InfinityFree (iceiy.com) hosting, cleartext HTTP
entries.detection: Block *.iceiy.com / *.yzz.me / *.zya.me / *.hstn.me — the InfinityFree free-hosting family is heavily reused by this Spanish-language Microsoft campaign

entries.technique: Free-hosting typosquat with ?i=1 step counter, same InfinityFree operator as the reactivar-* and verificarcuenta-* sites
entries.detection: Hunt hostnames matching (outlook|micros0ft|hotmail).*-?20(25|26) on free-hosting eTLDs; ?i=1 marks step 1 of this kit's flow

entries.technique: Zero-for-O typosquat ('0365') abusing GitBook's free docs hosting as a redirect/landing stage
entries.detection: Alert on digit-for-letter swaps (0365, micr0s0ft, 0nedrive) and on *.gitbook.io / *.gitbook.com hosts referenced in mail — SaaS doc platforms are current staging favorites

entries.technique: Weebly free-site 'mailbox validation' page with ticket-number padding in the hostname to look like a support case
entries.detection: Regex ^[0-9]{5,7}-.*(outlook|mailbox|office|validate).*\.weebly\.com$; Weebly/Webflow/Typedream subdomains carry no legitimate Microsoft auth

entries.technique: Double-brand lure — 'microsoft' subdomain on a Citrix ShareFile-style typosquat apex, document-share pretext
entries.detection: Alert on hostnames stacking two vendor brands (microsoft.<othervendor>-*.com); legitimate Citrix domains never host a microsoft.* label

entries.technique: Fake Outlook add-in/plugin distribution domain used to prompt for mailbox credentials and OAuth consent
entries.detection: Watch for Entra ID consent grants to non-verified publishers plus DNS to hostnames pairing 'outlook' with 'plugin/addin/connector'

entries.technique: ccTLD typosquat impersonating a French SharePoint tenant for shared-document credential capture
entries.detection: Alert on hyphenated brand pairs on ccTLDs (microsoft-sharepoint.*, onedrive-microsoft.*); real tenants always sit under sharepoint.com

entries.technique: 'Service update required' typosquat apex driving a fake M365 sign-in, fronted by Cloudflare
entries.detection: Block newly registered domains combining microsoft/m365/office with update(s)/alert(s)/notice; check RDAP creation date <30 days

entries.technique: SKU-name typosquat (licensing/renewal pretext) on IONOS hosting over cleartext HTTP
entries.detection: Hunt domains built from Microsoft SKU names (businessbasic, e3, e5, businesspremium); HTTP-only MS-branded hosts are high-confidence phishing

entries.technique: Fake licensing/support portal typosquat used as a vishing + credential-capture landing page
entries.detection: Flag domains concatenating office365/m365 with support|licensing|billing|renewal; correlate with inbound 'license expired' mail subjects

entries.technique: Fake Cloud Solution Provider support portal on a .digital typosquat; sibling of the already-tracked click2.* subdomain
entries.detection: Wildcard-block *.microsoftsupportcenter.digital — the apex is attacker-controlled and spins new subdomains (click2, csp, …) per wave

entries.technique: Country-code-flavored typosquat ('-se' Sweden) on a bulk-hosting IP shared with other Microsoft lookalikes
entries.detection: Shares 64.191.166.0/24 with microsoftuk.co — enumerate that netblock's reverse DNS for additional microsoft<cc> squats

entries.technique: Regional typosquat ('microsoftuk') on the same bulk host as microsoft-se.us, serving a cloned MS sign-in
entries.detection: Pattern-match microsoft<2-letter-cc> and microsoft-<cc> registrations; block the 64.191.166.0/24 cluster

entries.technique: Polish-targeted typosquat on the free biz.pl second-level domain
entries.detection: Treat *.biz.pl / *.waw.pl and similar free Polish SLDs as untrusted for any brand-bearing label; alert on 'microsoft' + locale suffix

entries.technique: Free eu.org subdomain typosquat behind Cloudflare, random two-letter suffix to evade string blocklists
entries.detection: Block *.eu.org for brand-bearing labels; alert on 'microsoft' + 1-3 random chars, a generator signature across this operator's domains

entries.technique: 'microsoft' subdomain on a Chinese update-themed apex, Cloudflare-fronted, cleartext HTTP
entries.detection: Alert on a 'microsoft' label as a subdomain of any non-Microsoft eTLD+1 — a simple, very high-signal rule for sign-in phishing

entries.technique: Brand-concatenation typosquat on a .social gTLD used as an Outlook webmail sign-in clone
entries.detection: Monitor new gTLD registrations (.social, .surf, .day, .beer) containing outlook/hotmail/onedrive — this actor favors cheap novelty TLDs

entries.technique: Entra ID OAuth path-clone — replicates /common/oauth2/v2.0/authorize on a throwaway .sbs domain with an 'office' host label
entries.detection: Alert on outbound HTTP to any non-microsoft TLD whose URI path contains '/common/oauth2/v2.0/authorize' — the path is unique to Microsoft identity endpoints and never legitimate off *.microsoftonline.com/*.microsoft.com

entries.technique: Full HTML clone of login.live.com (reuses genuine jsDisabled.srf endpoint and uaid/mkt/lc params) on attacker domain oauth-live.com
entries.detection: Hunt proxy/DNS for requests to '*.srf' URIs (ppsecure, jsDisabled.srf, GetCredentialType) on hosts outside login.live.com/login.microsoftonline.com; also pivot on any domain combining 'oauth' + 'live'

entries.technique: Typosquat/brand-combo domain (oauth-live.com) serving a 'login.' host that fronts the Microsoft Account sign-in clone
entries.detection: Block the apex oauth-live.com and alert on newly-observed domains matching regex (oauth|login|sso).*-?(live|msonline|microsoft) registered <30 days

entries.technique: Newly-registered (5-day-old) domain replicating the Teams sign-in screen and post-login Teams UI to harvest M365 credentials
entries.detection: Flag first-seen traffic to domains containing 'teams' on the .live/.cloud TLDs; correlate with brand-new WHOIS creation dates (<14 days) in your NRD feed

entries.technique: Victim-targeted subdomain of the teams-cloud.live Teams clone — org name prefixed as a subdomain for tailored lures (healthcare/pharma targeting)
entries.detection: Search DNS/SNI logs for your own company name appearing as the left-most label of an external domain (e.g. '<yourorg>.*'); that pattern is a reliable tailored-phish signal

entries.technique: Compromised legitimate website hosting an OWA sign-in kit under a /EN/owa/ directory
entries.detection: Alert on '/owa/' or '/exchange/' URI paths requested on external hosts that are not your own Exchange/Outlook namespaces

entries.technique: Compromised WordPress site — static outlook.html credential-harvest page dropped under /wp-content/uploads/ with randomized nested directories
entries.detection: Hunt web-proxy logs for '/wp-content/uploads/' paths ending in .html with Microsoft-brand filenames (outlook.html, myoffice.html, office365.html); uploads dirs should serve media, never HTML login forms

entries.technique: HTML credential-harvest page hosted in a public Backblaze B2 bucket (trusted-cloud hosting abuse); same 'myoffice.html' kit family as prior B2 buckets
entries.detection: Block/alert on *.backblazeb2.com '/file/*/*.html' object fetches from user endpoints — B2 buckets serving HTML to browsers is near-universally phishing in enterprise traffic

entries.technique: Cloudflare Workers-hosted 'shared document' lure chaining to an M365 sign-in prompt; hostname embeds victim-org and 'mcs365' strings
entries.detection: Alert on *.workers.dev hostnames containing document/share/drive/365/mcs tokens; most orgs can safely treat user-facing workers.dev as block-by-default with an allowlist

entries.technique: AiTM phishing-as-a-service portal replicating the Microsoft 'Pick an account' selection screen, victim keyed by GUID in the ?c= parameter
entries.detection: Hunt URIs matching '/accountselection(page)?/c?c=<guid>' on any non-Microsoft host — same kit template as the365notify.com cluster; pivot on the GUID to find sibling victim links

entries.technique: AiTM kit second-stage account-selection URL on the same safe365apps.com infrastructure (shorter ?c= victim token)
entries.detection: Block apex safe365apps.com; generically flag lookalike domains combining 'safe/secure/verify' + '365' + 'apps/login/auth'

entries.technique: Typosquat domain m365-microsoft.com with per-victim '/i/<32-hex>' tracking links; 'security.' subdomain used for account-security-alert lures
entries.detection: Regex-hunt '/i/[0-9a-f]{32}' URI paths across proxy logs and sinkhole the whole m365-microsoft.com zone (security., support., emailnotifications., programme-hup. all observed)

entries.technique: Free Korean shared-hosting (dothome.co.kr) subdomain typosquat ('outlook365livee') serving an Outlook webmail sign-in clone
entries.detection: Alert on *.dothome.co.kr and similar free-hosting wildcard zones where the subdomain label contains outlook/office/365/live — no legitimate business use in most environments

entries.technique: Typosquat domain mimicking the login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2 OpenID sign-in path, hosted on a cPanel default 'cpanel.site' hostname
entries.detection: Alert on DNS/proxy requests to *.cpanel.site whose FQDN contains 'microsoftonline' or 'signin-openid'; cPanel default hostnames embed the server IP with dashes (129-121-112-148)

entries.technique: Mail-themed subdomain of the same microsoftonline-com-common-signin-openid typosquat kit on shared cPanel infrastructure
entries.detection: Pivot on the parent domain microsoftonline-com-common-signin-openid[.]* via passive DNS — this actor spins up mail./v3sec. labels per target

entries.technique: Billing/licence-expiry lure on a long deceptive-label typosquat where 'login.microsoftonline' is placed in the subdomain, not the registrable domain
entries.detection: Regex URL hostnames for 'login\.microsoftonline' NOT followed by '\.com$' — a legitimate Microsoft sign-in host always terminates at login.microsoftonline.com

entries.technique: Per-victim random 8-char subdomain prepended to the microsoftonline-billing-verification typosquat (wildcard DNS) for link-uniqueness and sandbox evasion
entries.detection: Flag wildcard-DNS patterns: random 8-letter lowercase label + '.login.' + Microsoft-themed registrable domain; same kit on DigitalOcean IP 161.35.102.243

entries.technique: Operator test artifact of the same wildcard kit — 'test.' label stacked on the per-victim subdomain, confirming active kit development
entries.detection: Hunt for 'test.' / 'dev.' labels prefixed to phishing wildcard hosts; these surface the kit's staging URLs before the campaign goes live

entries.technique: Second per-victim wildcard subdomain of the billing-verification typosquat kit on the same 161.35.102.243 host
entries.detection: Block the whole registrable domain microsoftonline-billing-verification-secured-help rather than individual FQDNs; rotation is automated

entries.technique: Same kit on a second DigitalOcean node (104.248.114.136) with a 'www.' + random-label wildcard FQDN
entries.detection: Correlate TLS SNI logs for cpanel.site certificates issued to Microsoft-keyword hostnames; Certificate Transparency shows the wildcard issuance burst

entries.technique: Microsoft billing-verification credential harvester, wildcard subdomain variant on 104.248.114.136
entries.detection: Any inbound mail containing a URL whose hostname has 5+ dot-separated labels and includes 'microsoftonline' is high-confidence phish

entries.technique: Wildcard-DNS Microsoft 365 billing lure on shared cPanel hosting
entries.detection: Blocklist the two IPs 161.35.102.243 and 104.248.114.136 — both serve only this Microsoft-impersonating kit

entries.technique: Brand-keyword typosquat domain ('microsoft' + 'cloud verification') serving an account-verification credential prompt over plain HTTP
entries.detection: Newly-registered-domain rules on registrable domains starting with 'microsoft' that are not in Microsoft's own CT/WHOIS footprint (MarkMonitor registrar)

entries.technique: 'sso.' subdomain on a hyphenated microsoft-onedrive typosquat to imitate a federated single-sign-on endpoint for a OneDrive share lure
entries.detection: Flag hostnames with the label 'sso' or 'adfs' on any non-Microsoft-owned domain containing 'microsoft'; legitimate OneDrive SSO goes to login.microsoftonline.com only

entries.technique: ccTLD typosquat of Outlook webmail (.de) hosting a mailbox sign-in harvester
entries.detection: Monitor CT logs for certificates on 'outlook*' registrable domains across ccTLDs; block at the apex since mail./www. variants follow

entries.technique: 'mail.' subdomain of the outlookmails.de typosquat, presenting a fake Outlook mailbox login
entries.detection: Outbound POSTs to a host matching /outlook[a-z]*\.(de|fr|it|es)$/ with form fields named 'passwd'/'login' indicate credential submission

entries.technique: Free-hosting abuse — auto-generated Vercel subdomain (adjective-numeral naming) serving a cloned Outlook sign-in page
entries.detection: Alert on *.vercel.app / *.netlify.app / *.pages.dev hostnames beginning with 'outlook', 'microsoft', 'onedrive' or 'login'; legitimate Microsoft never hosts auth on PaaS preview domains

entries.technique: Second Vercel-hosted Outlook sign-in clone from the same operator naming scheme ('outlook-<word>')
entries.detection: Hunt proxy logs for Referer-less GETs to *.vercel.app followed by a POST — static-host phish kits exfiltrate to a Telegram/webhook endpoint on submit

entries.technique: Apex of the m365-microsoft[.]com typosquat used by an ongoing campaign that also rotates support./security./emailnotifications. subdomains with /i/<32-hex> per-victim tokens
entries.detection: Block the registrable domain m365-microsoft[.]com outright; hunt URL paths matching '/i/[0-9a-f]{32,33}' as a per-recipient tracking token signature

entries.technique: Regional-branding typosquat ('Microsoft Africa') on .org, a TLD Microsoft does not use for tenant sign-in
entries.detection: Flag 'microsoft-<region/country>' registrable domains; cross-check against Microsoft's authoritative domain list — all legitimate auth is on microsoft.com/microsoftonline.com/live.com

entries.technique: Compromised legitimate WordPress site hosting an Office 365 PHP phishing kit in an attacker-created directory ('linkmyGod/office-3D8')
entries.detection: Hunt web-proxy logs for '/index.php' under path segments containing 'office', 'o365' or 'owa' on otherwise unrelated business domains; kit directories are deployed via uploads/ or plugin RCE
